title: Scientists Find an Eyeless Snail Living in a Dark Chinese Cave
summary:
Scientists have discovered a new kind of tiny freshwater snail living deep inside a cave in China. It is the first freshwater cave snail ever recorded in the country.

The new species is named Erhaia dijiang. Because it spends its whole life in darkness, it has completely lost its eyes. Its cone-shaped shell is almost see-through, its body has no color, and it has long, thin feelers called tentacles.

The name comes from an old Chinese book of myths called the Classic of Mountains and Seas. It tells of Di Jiang, a mountain god shown as a beast with no face. The name fits, because the snail strongly avoids light. In the lab, the snails always moved into dark spaces under rocks when light shone on them.

The snail was found in a limestone cave about 2,062 meters, or roughly 6,800 feet, above sea level. That makes it the highest cave snail ever recorded in its family. The snails live among gravel and broken rocks in water less than one meter deep, where the temperature stays near 20 degrees Celsius. Scientists watched them eat diatoms, which are tiny algae that grow on rocks.

The discovery, published in the journal Subterranean Biology, helps scientists learn about underground water life in East Asia, which has not been studied much.

But the researchers are worried about the snail's future. During their search in August 2025, they found only three living adults and one empty shell, and no young snails. They said its outlook is "far from optimistic."

The team is asking for more surveys of caves across China and for quick action to protect these rare animals and their fragile homes.
why_it_matters: Discovering a species that may already be very rare shows how much is still unknown about underground ecosystems and why scientists want to protect them before species disappear.

background_read: Caves are dark, quiet places, and animals that live there all the time often lose their eyes and color over many generations because they no longer need them.
Many caves form in limestone, a rock that water slowly dissolves to make tunnels and pools.
When scientists find a new species, they describe it in a scientific journal and give it a two-part scientific name.
Animals that live in only one small place, like a single cave, can be at special risk because any change to that place affects the whole population.
